topology_reasoning.operation: A central input guide begins as the only left port. It narrows through a long linear adiabatic taper while two initially narrow, symmetrically offset rails broaden beside it. The two rails then use opposite S-bends to form well-separated output guides. The image therefore represents an adiabatic transfer/splitter, rather than a junction stencil.
observations: The central material track occupies x=0 to approximately 25 um and tapers from about 0.27 um to a tip around 0.04 um.
The upper and lower rails begin at approximately x=3 um with about 0.07 um width, widen linearly to about 0.244 um at x=25 um, and are initially offset by about +/-0.27 um from the input centerline.
The output rails retain the 0.244 um width while opposite smooth S-bends increase their centerline separation through approximately x=36 um; they then continue straight to x=40 um.
topology_reasoning.implementation: Use only gdsfactory straight/taper primitives plus gf.Path extruded rails for the smooth S-bends, assembled in an @gf.cell component on layer (1, 0).

iterations.change_made: First primitives-only assembly. Diff inspection found the input straight was erroneously 0.5 um wide because the supplied cross-section overrode its width argument; correct its cross-section width before the next deterministic comparison.

Corrected the input straight to 0.270 um. The diff then showed the central taper missing material toward its tip, rails about one pixel too wide on their outer edges, and S-bends beginning too early. Increase the central tip to 0.070 um, reduce rail width to the legal 0.242 um grid value, and add a 0.45 um rail straight before a correspondingly shorter smooth S-bend.

Applied the image-derived central-tip, rail-width, and delayed-S-bend corrections. This is the retained honest best: it exceeds the 0.85 Phase-A criterion and has exact calibrated 40.0 by 1.7 um bounds.
